A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the new interaction can be used to describe low-energy hadronic processes in the framework of CHPT q, which are not described by the current algebra approach or by the hadronic chiral Lagrangian approach with linear realization of the chiral U(2) × U(2) symmetry.
the low-energy hadronic interactions can be described by the effective chiral Lagrangeans with linear realization of symmetry at the hadronic and quark levels.

, within CHPTq, the low-energy hadronic interactions are governed by the following three kinds of interactions: (1) the standard interactions, which are produced by the standard Feynman diagrams with the standard constituent-quark loops, (2) the interactions produced by the box-constitutent-quark-loop diagrams and (3) the interactions produced from the box-constituient-quark-loop diagrams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the framework of CHPT q the low-energy AP 2 - and AP 3 -interactions are of the same order of magnitude.

the AP 3 -constituent-quarks-loop diagrams, which have been ignored in the current algebra approach and the effective hadronic Lagrangian approach, are convergent, and the new AP 3 -contributions are small and negligible in the case of low-energy pion-nucleon interactions and the pion-pion scattering.
the low-energy hadronic interactions, which are not included in the current algebra approach, are important for the description of low-energy processes.
